name: Standing Soleus Stretch
summary: A static lower-leg stretch performed with a bent knee to emphasize the soleus muscle and Achilles tendon.

setup: Stand facing a wall or sturdy support in a staggered stance with the target leg behind you.
Place both hands flat against the wall at chest height.
Point both feet directly forward and ensure the back heel is firmly planted on the floor.
steps: Bend both knees, lowering your hips straight down while keeping your back heel firmly on the ground.
Continue shifting your weight downward and slightly back until a gentle stretch is felt deep in the back calf and Achilles tendon.
Hold the position steadily for the desired duration without bouncing.
Carefully straighten the legs to exit the stretch, then switch sides.
instructions.breathing: Breathe smoothly and deeply throughout the hold, relaxing into the stretch on each exhalation.

common_faults.correction: Bend the rear knee to slacken the gastrocnemius and shift tension specifically to the soleus.

common_faults.fault: Lifting the rear heel off the ground.
common_faults.correction: Shorten the stance slightly so the rear heel remains firmly anchored to the floor.
Keep both feet parallel and facing straight ahead to maintain proper alignment across the ankle joint.

precautions: Avoid aggressive stretching if recovering from an acute Achilles tendon strain or rupture.
